Sisaket is a southern Isan province that lately got on the map for its volcanic-soil durian, grown on volcanic earth around Kantharalak and prized for a flavor all its own. When durian season hits, people drive straight to the orchards to eat it on the spot. The province also has old Khmer temples scattered across several districts, the Pha Mo I Daeng cliff and the trail up to Khao Phra Wihan along the border, and a mix of ethnic communities — Lao, Khmer, Suay, and Yoe — all living side by side. It's a place to take slowly, where you get nature, good food, and traces of history all at once.
